source.snippet: I'm implementing an API Export Restriction using Salesforce Shield Transaction Security Policy. The requirement is to block user API operations that process more than 200 records, while allowing certain internal/managed-package operations such as Salesforce CPQ to continue working. My current Transaction Security Policy uses conditions: Operation = QueryAll, Rows Processed >= 200, etc. The challenge is distinguishing CPQ's internal API calls from user-initiated bulk exports in Transaction Security policy logic.

problem_statement: Salesforce Shield Transaction Security Policies cannot easily distinguish CPQ or other managed-package internal API calls from user bulk-export operations, forcing admins into complex workarounds or accepting security gaps to keep CPQ functional.
target_segment: Salesforce admins and architects at mid-to-large enterprises running both Salesforce Shield and Salesforce CPQ, typically in regulated industries (finance, healthcare, manufacturing).
notes: Buyer signal: Salesforce Shield is a paid add-on (~$50/user/month); customers paying for Shield are typically enterprise accounts with active security/compliance budgets. CPQ is also a paid product. The friction here occurs at the intersection of two expensive paid products, meaning the customer has already demonstrated willingness to pay. Opportunity: a consulting playbook, automated policy template generator, or a lightweight managed package that injects traceable headers into CPQ API calls to make them distinguishable in Transaction Security rules.
